To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effectiveness of the non-union representative structures at Eurotunnel is questionable.
the effectiveness of employee voice at the Eurotunnel is questionable, and that union recognition through an agreement has also raised issues regarding the impact of unions at the Eurotunel.

1) the effectiveness of nonunion structures in representing employees is questionable; 2) union recognition through an Employer/Union partnership agreement has raised important issues regarding legitimacy of unions at ET; 3) the alignment of interests of employers with employees is more likely to occur when employers address employee concerns and give employees a greater say in decision-making processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of non-union employee voice structures in the transition to partnership.
the effectiveness of nonunion structures in representing employee interests.
how employers can encourage a greater degree of employee voice and how this can lead to improved employee commitment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the process of transition at Eurotunnel has been a process of transition from one form of employee voice to another, but not necessarily a process of transition to a better form of employee voice.
the outcomes of employee voice arrangements are highly variable.
the outcomes of non-union representative structures at Eurotunnel have been limited and have not resulted in a significant improvement in the relationship between the company and employees.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
employee voice can be an effective means of managing industrial relations in a non-union setting.

the employer needs to develop a more strategic approach towards the implementation of non-union representative structures and that such structures should be seen as a complement to union representation rather than as a replacement for it.
there is no one best way to represent employees.
The main takeaway from our work is that
employee engagement is a two-way process that requires a genuine commitment from employers to listen and act on employee concerns.

employee voice is an important part of the employment relationship and that employers should not underestimate the importance of employee voice in the development of effective employment relationships.
employers need to place greater trust in employee representatives and allow employees to be more involved in the decision-making processes.
